changes.before: Use a type check to choose arithmetic or preserved text.
changes.after: Check which kind of value you have before using it.

before: string | number allows either kind at a function boundary. Before an operation that needs one particular kind, check which kind you actually have. Narrowing is the checker using a runtime condition to learn a more specific type in that branch.

The input "04" does not become 4 just because its characters are digits. typeof distinguishes its actual runtime kind. No parsing is performed here. A condition about the value also helps the compiler allow only operations appropriate to that path.

Implement describeCount(value: string | number): string. For numbers return "Next " followed by value + 1; for text return "Label " followed by the unchanged text. Both supported input kinds must be accepted.
after: `string | number` allows text or a number. Narrowing means using a check to learn which type you have on one path through the code. That lets you use the right operation for that value.
`typeof` checks the actual kind of value. If the same function receives the text `"04"`, it returns Code 04. It keeps the leading zero because it does not turn the text into a number.
Make describeCount accept text or a number. For a number, return Next followed by a space and the number plus 1. For text, return Label followed by a space and the unchanged text.
